subject: Where LLM requests travel and which subprocessors touch data (Prospect Q&A)
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@medatlas.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify: processing locations and subprocessors for PII (MedAtlas)

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for taking this — quick Q from our security and legal leads as we evaluate Redwood for a pilot. High level we need to confirm where customer request data (prompt text and any uploaded artifacts) is processed, and which third parties (subprocessors) may see or process any derived data. Specifically: 

- Primary region(s) where inference and logs are executed/stored by default.
- Whether routing can cause data to leave that region (cross-border transfer) and under what conditions (failover, capacity).
- Subprocessors used for compute, monitoring, logging, analytics and backups (names and locations).
- Retention windows for transient caches, inference logs, and customer-stored artifacts.
- How deletion requests are handled and expected SLAs.

We will need documentary evidence (SOC2 summary, subprocessor inventory, any region maps) to feed into our vendor review.

If it's easier, happy to schedule a short technical call this week — our security manager (cc'd) will join.

Thanks,
Elena Ruiz
Senior Security Program Manager
MedAtlas

[Attached: vendor-whitelist.pdf (pdf, 120KB)]

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@medatlas.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, priya_natarajan@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify: processing locations and subprocessors for PII (MedAtlas)

Elena — thanks for the clear list. Short answer up front: Redwood can serve inference in region-local compute and provides a documented subprocessor inventory; routing can fall back to other compatible regions only under constrained capacity or outage, and we support contractual residency controls for pilots and private deployments. Below I outline specifics and attach a region map and our current subprocessor inventory CSV.

1) Primary processing locations
- Hosted (default): US (us-west-2 and us-east-1). For EU customers we offer region-local hosting (eu-west-1) by request.
- Dedicated/Private: customer can pin workload to a VPC region or on-prem.

2) Routing and cross-border transfers
- Smart routing policy: requests are routed by region, latency, and capacity. If the Preferred Region is available, we route there.
- Cross-border routing happens only for: planned bursts (customer-approved), unexpected capacity failure in region, or explicit routing policy configured by the customer.
- For customers requiring strict residency, we enforce \"region pinning\" on Dedicated/Private and include an operational SLA in the contract.

3) Subprocessors (overview)
- Compute: AWS (us-west-2, us-east-1), GCP (europe-west1) for EU-only customers; partner-managed clusters for private deployments.
- Storage/Logs: S3/Cloud Storage (same region as compute where possible).
- Monitoring & analytics: LogStream (US-based analytics vendor), Prometheus hosted by our infra partner.
- CDNs / edge: FastEdge (edge caching only, no persistent PII storage).

Full subprocessor names/locations are in the attached subprocessor-inventory.csv. Note: for any vendor that processes customer-provided content we can include them in the DPA.

4) Retention & deletion
- Transient inference caches (KV cache / prefix cache): default TTL is 1 hour and not written to long-term storage.
- Inference logs (request/response): default retention 30 days in hosted plans; Dedicated can be configured down to 0 days (audit logs still retained per SLA).
- Uploaded artifacts: stored in customer-isolated buckets with retention policy controlled by customer; deletion requests via API or Console trigger an asynchronous purge.
- Deletion SLAs: Hosted purge completes within 7 days (propagation across backups/caches may take up to 30 days for full removal from all redundant stores). Dedicated/private SLAs are defined in the commitment.

5) Evidence and next steps
- Attached: redwood-region-map.pdf (visual), subprocessor-inventory.csv (current).
- We also maintain a SOC2 summary and a signed DPA; can provide a SOC2 report under NDA and standard contract flow.

If you want, we can set up a 30-minute call with Marissa (Infrastructure PM) and Priya (Privacy/Legal) to walk through the subprocessor CSV and produce any addenda. Propose Wed 16 Jun 10:00 PT — does that work?

Best,
Jonas Weber
Head of Solutions 
Redwood Inference

[Attachments: redwood-region-map.pdf (pdf, 420KB); subprocessor-inventory.csv (csv, 12KB)]

Elena

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com <jonas_weber@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify: processing locations and subprocessors for PII (MedAtlas)

Elena — quick clarifications below and I've dropped the SOC2 summary and a redacted DPA stub in the Drive link. We'll bring Marissa and Priya to the call to get legal/tech answers recorded.

- LogStream: processes only aggregated telemetry by default. Raw prompts or outputs are not sent to analytics vendors in our standard hosted configuration. There is an opt-in diagnostic pipeline customers can enable for lab environments; that pipeline is always documented and must be explicitly enabled by a named admin (we don't enable it by default).

- Inference logs: by default we persist request metadata and token-level timing but not customer-assigned PII fields; customers can elect to persist request/response payloads for debugging. We recommend redaction at the application layer for PII.

- SOC2 / DPA: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf and a DPA redacted example are available at the Drive link below. For procurement we can provide the full SOC2 under NDA and execute a DPA with explicit subprocessor appendices.

Drive (already uploaded): https://drive.redwood.com/shared/MedAtlas/data-routing-evidence

Next steps: Please confirm three preferred time windows and we'll lock the meeting. Priya will be able to note any DPA redlines ahead of the call.

Regards,
Jonas
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
